question:
Which of the below has not undergone trisyllabic laxing during its sound development: 

southern, derivative, serenity, pleasant, gratitude, shadow

1.text:
In English the classic trisyllabic-laxing environment is a Latinate
stressed vowel that is followed by two or more unstressed syllables, 
e.g.

* derive /dɪˈraɪv/ > derivative /dɪˈrɪv.ə.tɪv/  /aɪ/ > /ɪ/
* serene /səˈriːn/ > serenity /səˈrɛ.nɪ.ti/  /iː/ > /ɛ/
* please /pliːz/ > pleasant /ˈplɛ.zənt/  /iː/ > /ɛ/
* grate /ɡreɪt/ > gratitude /ˈɡræ.tɪ.tuːd/  /eɪ/ > /æ/

and the same type of vowel reduction is what is normally quoted for
`divine` > `divinity`, `provoke` > `provocation`, etc. All four of the
Latinate items in the set show the familiar tense → lax vowel
reduction that is the phonetic reflex of the trisyllabic-laxing
process.

`southern` is a native Germanic compound `south` + `-ern`. The stressed
vowel of the base is the tense diphthong /aʊ/ ~ /ʌ/ in  `south` 
/ saʊθ / and it remains the tense diphthong /aʊ/ in 
`southern` /ˈsaʊ.ðən/ ~ /ˈsʌ.ðən/.  There is no development
/aʊ/ > * /ʊ/ or the like and the form never acquires the -V-V
environment that would trigger a trisyllabic laxation.  The same is
true in a very obvious way for the purely native disyllabic
`shadow` /ˈʃæ.doʊ/ which never had a tense stressed vowel to lax in
the first place.  That is the non-Latinate control case that is
normally quoted for the process.

3.text:
In English the “three–syllable rule’’ or trisyllabic laxing is the
shortening/laxing of a tense vowel in a stressed syllable that is
followed by two or more unstressed syllables, e.g.

* /iː/ > /ɪ/:  derive /dɪˈraɪv/ > derivative /dɪˈrɪv.ə.tɪv/
* /iː/ > /ɛ/:  serene /səˈriːn/ > serenity /səˈrɛ.nə.ti/
* /eɪ/ > /ɛ/:  ... etc.

The environment is therefore a polysyllabic word with a stressed
antepenultimate / penultimate syllable and at least two post-stress
syllables. 

* derivative /dɪˈrɪv.ə.tɪv/  < derive /dɪˈraɪv/
* serenity /səˈrɛ.nə.ti/ < serene /səˈriːn/
* gratitude /ˈɡræ.tɪ.tuːd/ is a trisyllabic -itude formation whose
initial stress vowel is the lax reflex of the Old French /aː/.

The three remaining items are disyllabic in Present-day English and
never enter the trisyllabic environment.  Of those the most
transparently non-derived native form is

shadow /ˈʃæ.doʊ/

a regular two-syllable OE sceadw.  It has no post-stress
bi-syllabic tail and its stressed vowel /æ/ is the historical short
a that it has always had. The same disyllabic status holds for
southern /ˈsaʊ.ðɚn/ ~ /ˈsʌ.ðɚn/ and pleasant /ˈplɛz.ənt/, both of
which are therefore also outside the classic trisyllabic laxing
environment.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: southern — Trisyllabic laxing regularly shortens a long/tensed vowel in the antepenultimate syllable, as in serene→serenity, derive→derivative, grateful→gratitude, and shade→shadow. In southern, however, the /ʌ/ is not the regular antepenultimate lax reflex of the vowel in south; it reflects Middle English shortening before the consonant cluster /ðr/ and later reduction of the final syllable. So the form that has not undergone trisyllabic laxing is southern.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: shadow is the odd one out.

Trisyllabic laxing / trisyllabic shortening is the shortening / laxing of a
stressed tense vowel when the stressed syllable is followed by two
unstressed syllables, e.g. /iː/ > /ɪ ~ ɛ/, /aɪ/ > /ɪ/, /eɪ/ > /ɛ/ etc.
in a derived / suffixed form.

* serene /səˈriːn/ > serenity /səˈrɛnəti/  /iː/ > /ɛ/
* derive /dɪˈraɪv/ > derivative /dɪˈrɪvətɪv/  /aɪ/ > /ɪ/
* please /pliːz/ > pleasant /ˈplɛzənt/  /iː/ > /ɛ/
* south /saʊθ/ > southern /ˈsʌðən/ ~ /ˈsaʊðən/
* grate /greɪt/ > gratitude /ˈɡrætɪtjuːd/  the stressed vowel is the
laxed reflex of the long base vowel

All of those are derived forms in which the base vowel is laxed / shortened
in the longer, trisyllabic / polysyllabic derivative. shadow /ˈʃædoʊ/
is a native disyllabic root with no trisyllabic derivative that shows the
regular /iː, aɪ, eɪ, oʊ/ > lax shortening alternation. It therefore has no
trisyllabic laxing history, in contrast to the derived set above. The
disyllabic items southern and pleasant are also non-trisyllabic in modern
phonology, shadow being the canonical non-derived root of the list.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: In the classic initial stress version of the change a long
stressed vowel is shortened / laxed when it is followed by two unstressed
syllables in the same word.  That is the environment that is normally
quoted as

photograph /ˈfəʊtəɡræf/ → photographer /fəˈtɒɡrəfə/ , 
polite /pəˈlaɪt/ → politeness /ˈpɒlɪtnəs/ etc.

In the set you give the only form which is really a trisyllabic
initially stressed word of that type is

gratu- i -tude /ˈɡrætɪtjuːd/

with <grate> /ɡreɪt/ > /ɡræt-/ before the two unstressed syllables –i–
tude.  Derivative /dɪˈrɪvətɪv/ and serenity /səˈrɛnəti/ show the same
phonetic shortening /aɪ/ > /ɪ/ and /iː/ > /ɛ/ ~ /ɪ/ but under non-initial
stress, i.e. a stressed vowel followed by two unstressed syllables on
the right.

Southern /ˈsʌðən/ ~ /ˈsaʊðən/, pleasant /ˈplɛzənt/ and shadow /ˈʃædoʊ/
are all disyllabic and therefore never meet the three-syllable
environment at all.  The vowel changes that they show, e.g. please
/iː/ > pleasant /ɛ/ and shade /eɪ/ > shadow /æ/, are the ordinary
closed-syllable / Great Vowel Shift shortening and not trisyllabic
shortening/laxing.  Shadow is the textbook disyllabic non-example; southern
and pleasant are in exactly the same class.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: shadow

In the strict phonological sense trisyllabic shortening / laxing is the shortening
of a stressed long vowel / diphthong to its lax counterpart when the stressed
syllable is followed by two or more unstressed syllables, i.e. in a
polysyllabic Latinate formation of the type

base Vː / V̆ > derived V̥ / V̆  / _ unstressed unstressed

derivative < derive /dɪˈraɪv/
 /dɪˈrɪv.ə.tɪv/   /aɪ/ > /ɪ/  riv is followed by ə-tɪv

serenity < serene /səˈriːn/
 /səˈrɛ.nə.ti/   /iː/ > /ɛ/ ~ /ɪ/  ren is followed by ə-ti

gratitude < *grat- /ˈgreɪt/
 /ˈɡræ.tɪ.tuːd/  the antepenultimate /aː/ ~ /eɪ/ of the Latinate
formation is the regular trisyllabic lax outcome, grat is followed by
ɪ-tuːd.

The three items that are in fact disyllabic Germanic / early Romance
forms can never be the environment for the rule.  Southern /ˈsʌð.ən/,
pleasant /ˈplɛz.ənt/ and shadow /ˈʃæ.doʊ/ are all two-syllable words,
the stressed vowel being followed by only one unstressed syllable, so
that there is no trisyllabic environment to trigger the shortening.
Shadow is the canonical clear non-Latinate, non-trisyllabic example of
the set, its /æ/ being the regular Old English sceadu reflex and not
a product of /aː/ > /æ/  or /eɪ/ > /ɛ/ trisyllabic laxing.  Southern and
pleasant are in the same disyllabic class.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: shadow is the odd one out.

The change that is normally called trisyllabic laxing is the
historical shortening/laxing of a long stressed monophthong in a
Romance loan in which the stress is followed by one or more unstressed
syllables, e.g.

* derive /dɪˈraɪv/  > derivative /dɪˈrɪvətɪv/  /aɪ/ > /ɪ/
* serene /səˈriːn/ > serenity /səˈrɛnəti/  /iː/ > /ɛ/
* please /pliːz/   > pleasant /ˈplɛzənt/  /iː/ > /ɛ/
* grate /ɡreɪt/    > gratitude /ˈɡrætɪtud/  /eɪ/ > /æ/

and the same shortening is visible in southern /ˈsaʊθ/ > /ˈsʌðən/ etc.
All of those are Classical borrowings in which a tense/long vowel that
is long in the disyllabic base is laxed/shortened in the polysyllabic
derived form.

*shadow* /ˈʃædoʊ/ < OE sceadu is native Germanic with an original short
/a/ ~ /æ/. It has no disyllabic or monosyllabic Romance base with a
historically long/tense vowel that is shortened in the polysyllabic
form, so it never participates in the regular trisyllabic
laxing/shortening of long monophthongs.  In surface terms it is also
only disyllabic, so the trisyllabic environment is never met.  That is
the contrast to derivative, serenity, pleasant and gratitude, which all
show the classic /iː/ > /ɛ/, /aɪ/ > /ɪ/, /eɪ/ > /æ/  Romance trisyllabic
laxing.  Southern is also morphologically disyllabic and its
/aʊ/ > /ʌ/ reduction is the ordinary unstressed vowel reduction of
south + -ern and not the monophthongal trisyllabic laxing proper.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: shadow. Trisyllabic laxing requires an originally long vowel that is shortened before following syllables. Shadow does not fit this: it goes back to Old English sceadu/sceadwe, where the first vowel was already a short breaking diphthong /æɑ/ before w, and the modern /æ/ is simply the continuation of that short vowel. The long vowel in shade arose later by Middle English open-syllable lengthening in a different form, so the shade/shadow contrast is not a genuine trisyllabic-laxing reflex. The other candidates are better explained by the usual historical shortening pattern.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: shadow

The set is a textbook illustration of pre-tonic / trisyllabic laxing
/ɪː/ /aɪ/ /eɪ/ /oʊ/ > /ɪ/ /ɪ/ /ɛ/ /æ/  etc. when a long stressed vowel is
followed by two or more unstressed syllables, the classic south → southern,
please → pleasant, grate → gratitude, etc. type.

* southern /ˈsʌðən/ < south /saʊθ/. The stressed /aʊ/ of the monosyllable is
laxed / centralised in the disyllabic derivative.
* pleasant /ˈplɛzənt/ < please /pliːz/. /iː/ > /ɛ/ before the unstressed
- ant.
* gratitude /ˈɡrætɪtjuːd/ < grate /ɡreɪt/ ~ grateful /ˈɡreɪtfəl/. /eɪ/ >
/æ/ in the trisyllabic, initially stressed form.
* derivative /dɪˈrɪvətɪv/ < derive /dɪˈraɪv/ and
serenity /səˈrɛnəti/ < serene /səˈriːn/. /aɪ/ > /ɪ/ and /iː/ > /ɛ/ in the
polysyllabic extensions, the normal pre-tonic shortening that is usually
described as trisyllabic laxing.

shadow is the non-example.  Shadow < OE sceadu is cognate with shade <
OE sceadu. The monosyllabic form shade underwent the regular Middle English
Great Vowel Shift /aː/ > /eː/ > /eɪ/, hence ModE /ʃeɪd/. The polysyllabic
shadow retained the older short /a/ reflex, /ʃædoʊ/. The vowel difference
is therefore the opposite of laxing: the simple form raised, the complex
form is conservative. It is the classic shade / shadow Great Vowel Shift
pair, not a case of trisyllabic laxing of a vowel that was long in the
monosyllable.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The genuine trisyllabic laxing environment is a stressed vowel that is followed by two or more unstressed syllables, the classic Latinate /iː/>/ɪ/, /uː/>/ʊ/, /eɪ/>/ɛ/, /oʊ/>/ɔ/ shortening that you get with -ity, -ive, -ation etc.

* derivative  /dɪˈrɪvətɪv/ < derive /dɪˈraɪv/  /aɪ/>/ɪ/
* serenity   /səˈrɛnəti/ < serene /səˈriːn/   /iː/>/ɛ/

are textbook trisyllabic laxing.  Pleasant /ˈplɛzənt/ < please /pliːz/ is the same vowel quality shift and gratitude /ˈɡrætɪtjuːd/ is a trisyllabic Latinate formation.

Shadow /ˈʃædoʊ/ is a disyllabic Germanic stem with no -ity/-ive/-ant
suffixation and no history of a long stressed vowel being shortened
by the trisyllabic environment. The same syllable-count objection
holds for the disyllabic southern /ˈsʌðən/ and for the disyllabic
pleasant, which is why those forms are normally quoted as outside the
proper trisyllabic laxing environment. Shadow is the clear non-Latinate,
non-trisyllabic example.
